claim: status: "operating" in rescue.json, and the audit_md/founder_md premise that this is a live business to contact
problem: A public bankruptcy record lists a Chapter 7 (liquidation) petition filed 31 July 2026 by "Molnar Roofing, Inc." in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey, case 26-18658, trustee Daniel E. Straffi, docket entries 31 Jul - 17 Aug 2026 (https://whofiledbankruptcy.com/case/njb/26-18658/, and the same entry in that site's NJ index: https://whofiledbankruptcy.com/court/njb/). The page does not print the debtor's address, so I could not confirm the 513 3rd Ave entity by address, and CourtListener/Justia/PACER could not be opened from here (CAPTCHA/403/per-page login) to check the official docket. Even unconfirmed, the exact company name in the same state makes this a closure signal the audit never looked for: rescue.json's data_gaps mention Yelp, YellowPages, BuildZoom and Google, but not bankruptcy or state registration, and the audit still set status "operating". The timing also fits - the site came off the domain between Nov 2025 and Jul 2026, and no review newer than 2019 was found anywhere. Sending the "Hi Steve ... your website link shows an error" email or the walk-in opener to a company in Chapter 7 liquidation would be a real error.
fix: Before any outreach: check case 3:26-bk-18658 on PACER (or ask a court runner), and check the NJ business entity record for Molnar Roofing Inc, to confirm whether the debtor is the 513 3rd Ave roofer. If it is, mark the business closed, drop it from the rescue list, keep the audit internal, and do not contact. If it is not, record that check with its URL in data_gaps and only then treat status as operating.

claim: audit_md: a GoDaddy parking page "passes visitors to a third-party ad page"
problem: What a visitor actually lands on is a third-party article page (dot-services.org, psystem=PW) that returns "Access Denied", so no advertisement was ever displayed to the auditor. Calling it an "ad page" is an inference stated as observed fact (rescue.json hedges to "article/ad page"; audit_md does not).
fix: Say "a third-party article page that returns 'Access Denied'", or add "(looks like an ad page, but it would not load)".

claim: audit_md: "The registration is paid to 6 August 2027"
problem: RDAP gives an expiration date, not a payment record. "Paid to" overstates the source (the audit's own inference block correctly says only "expires").
fix: "The domain is registered through 6 August 2027 (expiry date on the public registry record)".

claim: founder_md: "Hi Steve," and open questions about what "Steve" wants; walk-in opener
problem: The only source for the name is a Dec 2019 BestProsInTown review that refers to the roofer as Steve; nothing on the Google profile, Birdeye, CLAD or the archived site confirms he is the current owner or still there. It is an unlabelled inference used in a first-contact message.
fix: Add to open questions that the name is unconfirmed (from a 2019 review) and use "Hello" / "Hi there" in the draft until the owner is confirmed.

claim: fix step 2: the archived copy's text is "theirs to reuse"
problem: Reasonable but not stated by any source - ownership of the archived text is assumed, not shown, and the archive is a third-party copy.
fix: Hedge it ("use the archived copy as a reference for their own wording") or have them write fresh copy and treat the archive as a prompt.
